clue.text: Drawing of old Britisher with flower

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Britain
crossword 'flower' is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A sketch of an ancient Briton holding a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like a bloom but is read as flow-er, a river: the Ure in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing is a kind of image or illustration on paper.

clue.text: Gapes, travelling with us and seeing this constellation

indicators.note: the letters travel about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stares open-mouthed, travelling with us to see a star pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' rearranges only GAPES, giving PEGAS; 'with' joins US on unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged horse is a star group in the northern sky.

clue.text: Lure needed to get member to church

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Bait is needed to attract a member of the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' is a limb, not a churchgoer.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm is to entice or attract.

clue.text: Wave breaking up duel with tuna

indicators.note: breaking up the words signals rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A wave breaks up a fight with a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripple or move up and down like water is to undulate.

clue.text: Young bird of prey ascending

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Young bird of prey ascending (4)': EYAS is defined but no clue words supply letters to reverse; the fodder appears to be missing

clue.text: Bird pig's chasing around enclosure

indicators.note: the pig word goes around the enclosure word, wrapping it on both sides

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a wall encloses a garden or yard

explanation.surface: A bird is being chased by a pig round a farmyard pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' at the start invites a hunt for a bird in the wordplay; it is the definition, and the pig wraps the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: The swallow is a fork-tailed migrant songbird.

clue.text: Uttered by the bank-clerk?

parts.note: things a person says aloud, and also the account summaries a bank sends out

explanation.surface: What a bank cashier says.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken remarks share their name with a bank's account summaries.

clue.text: Volunteer force, sent up food, gets fit

indicators.note: in a down clue sending up reads the piece from bottom to top

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
tack is food, as in hardtack

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers send up food and get fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like healthy but is a sudden bout, as of coughing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden bout of illness, such as a heart seizure, is a fit.

clue.text: A judge with debts holding credit to be absurd

parts.note: m'lud, my lord, is how a judge is addressed

indicators.note: the debts word holds the credit abbreviation inside it

parts.note: IOUs are notes of debt

explanation.surface: A judge in debt but with credit seems absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is only the article; LUD is the courtroom form of address 'm'lud'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridiculous and absurd are synonyms.

clue.text: Strongly-built person taking clique to the spa

parts.note: a spa is a well of mineral water
a set is a clique, a social group

explanation.surface: A muscular person takes his crowd to the spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking clique to the spa' attaches SET to WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturdy, firmly made person is described as robust.

clue.text: A relative's here — and grappa's brought out

indicators.note: the letters are drawn out into a fresh arrangement, so this signals a rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A family member is here, and the Italian brandy has been produced.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's here' after 'relative' is a link; the brandy is pure fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandfather, in an old-fashioned affectionate form, is a family member.

clue.text: Boy, carrying article going west, in these waters?

indicators.note: in an across clue westward is right to left, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy
an article is a thing, an it

explanation.surface: A lad carries something westward across the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns the whole charade round, not one piece; 'carrying' simply joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal seas that rise and fall with the moon's pull are described with this adjective.

clue.text: Specimen that's more than enough

parts.note: the 's of that's supplies the letter S
ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: A specimen is described as being plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample is a representative piece taken for testing.

clue.text: At the summit, an animal heard, then birds

indicators.note: the words are spoken, so the answer only sounds like the pieces

parts.note: at the summit is at the peak; an ox is an animal

explanation.surface: A mountain-top creature makes a noise, followed by some birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' says PEAK + OX, spoken quickly, gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Peafowl males, famed for their fanned tails, are large showy birds.

clue.text: He scores a double-century for Taunton, surprisingly

indicators.note: double means the century letter appears twice over

parts.note: C is a hundred in Roman numerals

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters fall in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A batsman scores two hundred for Taunton, a cricket ground, unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Taunton is home of Somerset county cricket, so 'scores' looks like runs; the definition reads 'he keeps the score', i.e. counts money.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookkeeper keeps a tally, or score, of figures.

clue.text: Perched on a bridge, providing good viewing

definitions.meaning: glasses sit on the bridge of the nose
grand shows give an audience something worth watching

explanation.walkthrough: The 'bridge' is the nose's, not a river crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeglasses rest on the nose; the same word means impressive public shows.

clue.text: English river fish the French will find abhorrent

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a crab is a shellfish
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An English river fish is found disgusting by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Abominable and detestable are synonyms.

clue.text: Entertainer for the crowd

definitions.meaning: one who holds a party and receives guests

explanation.definitionFit: One who receives guests entertains them; a great number of people is a multitude, as in a heavenly throng.

clue.text: Writer figures on seeing chain of hills

indicators.note: in a down clue the figures come on, below, the writer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
nines are numerals, figures

explanation.surface: A writer works on figures while looking at a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: England's backbone, a long range of uplands in the north.

clue.text: Should you break this, your pocket won't be affected

definitions.text: Should you break this, your pocket won't be affected

parts.words: Should you break this, your pocket won't be affected
parts.note: to break this in business is to end with neither profit nor loss, so your money is unchanged

explanation.surface: Breaking something, but your wallet is untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking level means making neither gain nor loss.

clue.text: Amber changing to green light — yet causing a stoppage

indicators.note: the word amber changes into a new arrangement

parts.note: a green light means go

explanation.surface: A traffic light turns from amber to green, yet traffic stops.
explanation.walkthrough: The traffic-light surface hides that 'Amber' is fodder rearranged to EMBAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An official ban on trade is a stoppage.

clue.text: Four locks reportedly required for citadels

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the answer sounds like the pieces

parts.note: the number word, said aloud; locks of hair are tresses

explanation.surface: Four hairdos are needed to make strongholds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means FOUR + TRESSES, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Citadels are strongholds, fortified places.

clue.text: Prominent foreigner in the street

indicators.note: the foreigner is placed in the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: A notable foreigner stands out in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means standing out, conspicuous.

clue.text: The drawing room?

parts.note: not a lounge but a room where an artist draws

explanation.surface: The formal sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's workplace is where drawing gets done.

clue.text: Taking to task — for dropping tin-opener in the sea

indicators.note: the pieces are put inside the sea's name

parts.note: the Bering Sea lies between Alaska and Siberia
for can mean 'a', as in five pounds a head

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Scolding someone for throwing the tin-opener overboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' gives A (as in 'a head'), 'tin-opener' gives T, and 'dropping ... in' places AT inside BERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Berating means scolding or rebuking.

clue.text: Book for a yearly event

definitions.meaning: a book published once a year

explanation.definitionFit: A children's yearbook of stories is published once a year; something yearly happens every twelve months.

clue.text: One gets support from English ally

indicators.note: in a down clue the support sits beneath, so the second piece comes below

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: Someone gets backing from an English partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ally' is a verb here: join together.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to join forces, to combine.

clue.text: A border rising and Moslem leader's here

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word reads upward

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A border goes up and a Muslim leader is here.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir, also spelt this way, is a Muslim ruler or commander.

clue.text: Frenzied pincer-attack on bridgehead

indicators.note: a pincer movement closes in on both sides, so the attack word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a raid is an attack
the head, first letter, of bridge is B

explanation.surface: A frenzied two-pronged assault on a bridgehead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pincer' closes RAID round B; 'attack' looks military with 'bridgehead' but supplies the raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means wildly fanatical, as if maddened.

clue.text: A row about person holding daughter's jewellery

indicators.note: the row word goes around, about, the person and daughter

parts.note: a row is a line
a man is a person
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A quarrel about someone holding his daughter's jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line; 'about' puts it round MAN with D held.
explanation.definitionFit: Almandine is a deep red garnet used as a gem.

clue.text: Expand! Put one shot beyond the circle

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after, beyond, the circle

parts.note: a circle is the shape O

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An instruction to expand, and to place a shot outside the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' and 'shot' sound like shot-putting, but 'shot' signals the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread out or unfold is to make larger.

clue.text: Regard shape-changing spectre!

indicators.note: the ghost changes shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ghost that changes its form is held in esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Regard as esteem is high opinion or admiration.
